Article Title: Meta needed data from thousands of its employees for edge in AI space, company introduced Model Capability Initiative; but then came a very 'human problem'
Article Text:
Meta needed data from thousands of its employees for edge in AI space, company introduced Model Capability Initiative; but then came a very 'human problem'

Why Meta wanted employee data

Employees immediately pushed back

​

Then came the data leak

Meta found an internal way to get its hands on more data to strengthen its position in the artificial intelligence (AI) race. To bridge the data gap that didn't come from the internet, the social media giant was turning to its own employees. Meta’s elite AI unit, known as TBD, introduced the Model Capability Initiative (MCI), a programme designed to collect data on how thousands of employees use their computers.The idea was simple: keystrokes, mouse movements and screen activity could help AI models learn how humans actually work with computers. But Meta soon ran into a very human problem: opposition from its own employees. What followed was a rebellion involving memes, flyers and a petition signed by more than 1,800 workers.MCI was ‘invented’ by Meta because of the fundamental drawbacks that their AI systems had. Although the AI software is skilled in certain domains such as programming and research, it has not been able to perform basic computer tasks.According to people familiar with the project, Meta believed that training AI on employee data would help the systems understand how people actually do things. MCI was conceived in TBD, an AI research lab of about 100 people, which is seen as one of Meta's most advanced AI labs.When Meta announced MCI internally in April, the response fell far short of what the company expected.Employees raised concerns that the programme would capture sensitive information from their computers, including passwords, immigration documents and credit card details. Some also worried that the data could eventually be used to automate jobs currently performed by Meta employees.The backlash quickly spread through internal channels. Employees shared anti-MCI memes, while the recording icon was mockingly referred to as the “Eye of Sauron”.An internal petition opposing the programme eventually collected more than 1,800 signatures. Employees also distributed flyers at Meta offices and put up messages protesting the initiative.At first, Meta gave workers the option to opt out for 30 minutes in June so they could do personal business. Nonetheless, activists found it insufficient and demanded that Meta cancel MCI.However, MCI took its biggest blow toward the end of June. It emerged that data collected using the software was visible throughout Meta and even included private conversations. The leak became an instant viral sensation within Meta, seemingly confirming employees' fears about tight control of the data.Meta subsequently switched off MCI within hours. The company said it had suspended the programme and would make it opt-in if it brought it back. Two months later, it remained suspended.Uncertainty also remained over whether the collected data had actually been used to train Meta’s latest AI models. A manager reportedly said in July that it had not been used, while Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth told employees that the data was more useful than expected.
Article Summary: Meta introduced Model Capability Initiative (MCI) to collect data on how its employees use their computers. Employees raised concerns that the programme would capture sensitive information from their computers, including passwords, immigration documents and credit card details. Some also worried that the data could eventually be used to automate jobs.

Article Title: Apple rolls out its biggest iPhone software update of 2026: 10 ways iOS 27 will 'change' your iPhone
Article Text:
Apple's iOS 27 is out for iPhone 11 and newer, with Siri AI as the headline change.

iOS 27 compatible iPhones: the list stretches back to 2019

iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max

The complete iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 lines, including the 16e and 17e

iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo

iPhone SE, second generation onward

How to update to iOS 27

Back up first through Settings, your name, iCloud Backup, Back Up Now. Use a computer instead if your iCloud storage has run out.

Open Settings, General, Software Update. Swipe down on the page if iOS 27 is not showing yet.

Select iOS 27 and follow the prompts. A number of users have watched the installer describe itself as 26.7 before the phone reboots onto iOS 27.

Switch Siri AI on afterwards in Settings. It stays off until you ask for it, and it is not available to anyone under 13.

Siri AI knows what is in your inbox, and answers from it

Finding a mail, message, photo, link or file by person, date or place

Building a home automation from an instruction such as locking every door at midnight

Adding a birthday or a second number to a contact without opening the app

Lifting every ingredient off a recipe page into a shopping list

Answering questions about whatever is on screen, and searching the web when it has to

Point the camera at a restaurant bill and Siri splits it

Write with Siri copies your tone before it writes a word

Older iPhones feel quicker, and Liquid Glass gets a dial

Shortcuts builds the automation from one sentence

Photos can extend a shot past the edges of the frame

Safari watches a product page and tells you when the price falls

AirPods finally get a custom EQ, alarms get their own volume

A child now has to ask before opening a new website

Ask to Buy holds every app install until a parent says yes

Ask to Browse does the same for new websites in Safari, with the request arriving in the parent's Messages

Communication Safety, which already caught nudity, now intervenes on gore and violence in shared images and video

Time Allowances cap daily use across Entertainment, Games and Social Media, with age guidance Apple developed with clinical and child development specialists, while Schedules decide which apps work at which hours

One phone number across two iPhones, for a monthly fee

The smaller iOS 27 changes are the ones you will stumble into

Save a single frame from a video as a photo, instead of screenshotting and cropping it. Anyone who shoots video of moving children or pets has wanted this for years.

A Captured By Me filter in Photos separates pictures you actually took from the flood of forwards in your library, reaching back across older iPhones.

Wallet builds a pass from a photograph of a physical card, so a library card or a gift voucher stops living in a drawer. There is a manual template route if your iPhone does not support Apple Intelligence.

Home screen widgets stretch to an extra large size, which makes Notes, Calendar and Weather worth reading rather than tapping through. Weather now shows nine days instead of five.

Choose which eight controls sit above the Camera viewfinder. Lens Aperture and Shutter Speed are reserved for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.

Messages stops holding up your next text while a large photo crawls out over weak cellular.

Apple has released iOS 27, the largest iPhone software update it has shipped all year, and it is free for every iPhone 11 and newer. The rollout started on Monday and the update is live in India now. The headline is Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant that holds a proper back and forth, reads what is on your screen, and searches your own mail, messages and photos before it answers. Underneath that sit a Camera app that can read a restaurant bill, a Shortcuts app you can talk into shape, a Photos editor that pushes a picture past its own borders, and a slider for everyone who spent the last year quietly resenting Liquid Glass.Siri AI is also the feature Apple has owed its users since 2024. The personalised, context aware assistant it demonstrated that year never shipped on schedule, and the gap was long enough that a fair number of iPhone owners stopped waiting and installed a chatbot instead. What arrives today is that promise, delivered late and still carrying a beta label, with English first and French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish following in October.Apple has hedged the rest of the release accordingly. A great deal of engineering in iOS 27 has gone into things that have nothing to do with AI, from app launch times to how the phone hands over between Wi-Fi and cellular, which is the part of this update that will reach the most people.iOS 27 installs on:Apple Intelligence and Siri AI need a shorter list: iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, every iPhone 16 model and later, the iPhone Air and the iPhone Duo. A handful of features sit on an even narrower shelf. Tuning how Siri sounds, down to pitch and pace, is restricted to the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, Duo, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max and Air.The new assistant works like a chatbot with one thing no rival has, which is private access to what is already on the phone. When you install the update it indexes your calendar invites, mail, texts, files and notes, then answers from that. Ask for a recent photo of your dog and it surfaces several. Ask which weekend you were in Goa and it knows, because your boarding passes told it. The working list includes:Say the wake word and a shimmering orb appears in the Dynamic Island with a card you can pull down into a full Siri app, which keeps your conversations and continues them on an iPad. It now asks which part of a request it did not follow rather than failing silently. It is still slower to respond than Gemini, and it fumbles retrievals a well indexed inbox should make easy.Swipe past Photo and Video in the Camera app and a Siri tab appears. Hold it over a nutrition label and the numbers go into Health. Hold it over a shopfront and ask for the hours. Hold it over an event schedule and each entry lands in your calendar. The demo everyone will run is the receipt split, which reads the bill, works out each person's share with tax and tip, and settles the total through Apple Cash. Printed receipts scan reliably. Handwriting is a gamble. The Apple Cash requirement also means this is a feature Indian users can admire and not use.Siri can draft inside any text field, rewrite what you have typed, shift the register, or tell you where a draft is weak. In Messages and Mail it reads your existing writing and imitates your phrasing and punctuation, which is the difference between a useful draft and one you delete. Grammar suggestions now appear alongside spelling corrections across the system.Apple's own testing puts app launches up to 30 per cent faster, newly shot photos loading up to 70 per cent faster in the library, and AirDrop transfers up to 80 per cent faster. Treat the figures as the company's, but the change registers within minutes, and it lands on every supported handset instead of only the Apple Intelligence tier. Messages retries a failed send by itself now, and the switch between Wi-Fi and cellular is less jarring. For the look of the thing, Settings, Appearance, Liquid Glass opens a slider that runs from ultra clear to fully tinted.Shortcuts has always been capable and almost nobody used it, because building anything meant stacking actions by hand and guessing at the logic. Now you tap the plus sign, write what you want, and the app assembles it. Message a family member your ETA when you leave the office, or trigger a playlist when CarPlay connects. You can refine the result in plain language or edit the steps yourself.Clean Up has been the softest of Apple's editing tools since it launched, mostly because it left warped patches behind. It now runs in three modes: Fast, on device, for small removals, High Quality, which goes to Apple's servers, and Auto. Beside it are Extend, which invents what lies past the original frame, and Spatial Reframing, which shifts the apparent camera position after the picture was taken. Image Playground handles photorealistic output now, and Apple has said SynthID watermarking support is coming later this year.Notify Me is the smartest small idea in this release. Find the listing in Safari, open the Tab bar menu, tap Notify Me, describe the change you are waiting for and set how often the browser should check. It watches the page for a restock or a price cut and alerts you. Safari also sorts open tabs into topics on its own, and will write a custom extension from a plain description, from a citation generator to forcing a minimum font size on a site with unreadable type.You can tune the lows, mids and highs on AirPods yourself rather than accepting Apple's preset, through AirPods settings, Audio and Routing, Equaliser, Custom. It works on AirPods 4 and 5, AirPods Pro 2 and 3, and AirPods Max 2. Separately, Settings, Sounds and Haptics lets you unlink alarm volume from ringer volume, which fixes the old problem of sleeping through an alarm or being startled by a notification at maximum volume. GymKit also arrives on iPhone, and AirPods Pro 3 can pass heart rate data into a workout.The parental controls are the most substantial non AI work in this release, and they are built around approval rather than blocking:Screen Time itself has been redesigned around an at a glance view of what a child actually used.Two iPhones running iOS 27 can share a single number, with the line following whichever handset you unlock. It is set up in Settings, Cellular, This iPhone and Another. The obstacle is the carrier. Only T-Mobile supports it at launch, at roughly Rs 440 a month, with Verizon expected later this year and no Indian operator involved yet.Some of the best work in this update never made a slide. These are the fixes that remove a daily irritation rather than add a headline, and most of them land on older iPhones too.The bigger leftovers come with conditions attached. Call Context surfaces a confirmation code or a booking reference from your mail while you are on a call to a business. HomeKit Secure Video cameras record and stream in 4K, and the Home app can describe what happened in a clip or search footage in plain language, although those AI pieces need a 2TB iCloud+ plan for a single camera and more beyond that. Maps Flyover renders architectural detail and individual trees from aerial imagery. Cycle Tracking in Health adds perimenopause support, with deviation notifications aimed at users over 40. iCloud Shared Albums allow full resolution sharing at last, and are easier to join from Android or Windows. VoiceOver and Magnifier both pick up substantial accessibility work.One to wait for rather than look for: the Passwords app will update weak or compromised logins on your behalf, but Apple has marked that as coming in a future release rather than shipping it today.
Article Summary: Apple has released iOS 27, the largest iPhone software update it has shipped all year. It is free for every iPhone 11 and newer, and the update is live in India now. The headline change is Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant that holds a proper back and forth, reads what is on your screen, and searches your own mail, messages and photos before it answers.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.

Article Title: In 1853, Mumbai saw India's first commercial passenger train leave Bori Bunder for Thane; how a 1-hour-15-minute steam ride began country's rail legacy
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

A grand beginning in Bombay

From Bori Bunder to Thane

The beginning of Mumbai's railway legacy





Long before Mumbai's suburban trains became the lifeline of millions, the city's railway journey began with a 34-km steam-powered ride to Thane. On April 16, 1853, India's first commercial passenger train left Bori Bunder in Bombay, marking the beginning of a railway network that would eventually connect cities, towns and villages across the country. The train, operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR), carried around 400 passengers in 14 carriages. It travelled from Bori Bunder, near present-day Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, to Thane. The journey covered about 21 miles, or 34 km.The launch was treated as a major public event. April 16 was declared a public holiday in Bombay, allowing people to witness the arrival of a new form of transport. Large crowds gathered around Bori Bunder to see the train depart. At the inauguration, a 21-gun salute accompanied the departure, adding a ceremonial touch to what would become one of the most consequential developments in India's transport history. The train was made up of 14 passenger coaches and was initially documented as being hauled by three steam locomotives named Sahib, Sindh and Sultan. Contemporary and historical accounts put the journey time at around 1 hour and 15 minutes.For people watching from the sides of the railway line, the sight was unlike anything they had seen before. The steam locomotive, coaches and crowds marked the arrival of a technology that would eventually transform how people travelled across the subcontinent.The railway line between Bombay and Thane was only a modest beginning. The 34-km route connected the growing port city with Thane and demonstrated how rail transport could make movement of people and goods faster and more organised. The Great Indian Peninsula Railway would go on to expand its network beyond this first stretch. The railway system eventually became an important part of Bombay's growth, connecting the city to industrial areas and towns across the region. The route also laid the foundation for the railway system that would become central to Mumbai's identity. What began with a few hundred passengers on a short steam journey would eventually evolve into one of the world's busiest suburban railway systems.The 1853 journey is now regarded as the formal beginning of passenger rail services in India. Indian Railways' own historical material records April 16, 1853, as the date when the first passenger train travelled from Bombay to Thane with 14 coaches and around 400 passengers. There is, however, an important distinction in the history. The 1853 journey was not the first time a train had operated anywhere in India.Earlier railway experiments and trains had been used for purposes such as transporting construction material. What made the Bombay-Thane journey significant was that it marked the beginning of commercial passenger railway service in the country. More than 170 years later, Mumbai's railway network bears little resemblance to the railway that left Bori Bunder in 1853. Yet the city's daily railway story still traces its roots to that 34-km journey. From a steam train carrying around 400 passengers to today's packed suburban services carrying millions, Mumbai's relationship with its railways has grown alongside the city itself.
Article Summary: On April 16, 1853, India's first commercial passenger train left Bori Bunder in Bombay. The train, operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR), carried around 400 passengers in 14 carriages. The journey covered about 21 miles, or 34 km. The railway system became an important part of Bombay's growth.

Article Title: Norway’s Green Mountain data centre uses 8°C fjord water to cool its servers, turning a naturally cold resource into free refrigeration
Article Text:
How data centre cooling keeps servers running safely

How 8°C fjord water cools the data centre

PC: Green Mountain

How the cooling system uses gravity and recycled water

What PUE reveals about data centre energy use

How Green Mountain keeps its cooling system protected

How Green Mountain keeps its cooling system efficient

How 330 days of free cooling works at Rjukan

How the Rjukan cooling system scales with server demand

A data centre quietly produces heat every second it is operating. Behind the walls, rows of servers process data continuously, turning large amounts of electricity into computing power and, inevitably, excess heat. That heat has to be removed to keep the equipment within safe operating temperatures, adding significantly to the facility’s energy demand. Green Mountain has approached the problem differently at its Norwegian sites, using the country's naturally cool conditions as part of the cooling infrastructure. At one facility, water drawn from a nearby fjord remains at about 8°C at depth. Instead of making cold mechanically, engineers use this naturally chilled water to carry heat away.Servers turn electricity into computing power, but a large share of that energy eventually becomes heat. Keeping temperatures within operating limits therefore becomes a permanent requirement, with cooling systems running alongside the IT equipment.Green Mountain says conventional data centre cooling can require an additional 40 to 80% of the electricity used to power the servers. That makes the cooling system an important part of a facility's total energy performance, particularly at sites operating continuously.The company uses what is commonly called free cooling, or natural cooling. The basic idea is straightforward: instead of producing cold through energy-intensive mechanical refrigeration, the facility makes use of naturally cold air or water already available outside.At Green Mountain's SVG-Rennesøy site, the cooling source is the fjord immediately beside the data centre. The location has a particular underwater structure. The entrance to the fjord is relatively shallow, while the central section reaches considerable depth.Reportedly, at depths below roughly 75 metres, the water stays at about 8°C. Green Mountain installed intake pipes reaching down to around 100 metres, allowing the facility to access that cold water throughout the year.The water does not simply flow through the server rooms. Instead, it enters a cold-water basin and passes through a titanium heat exchanger. Heat from the data centre's separate chilled-water circuit is transferred to the cold seawater, which is then returned to the fjord.That arrangement keeps the two water systems separate.There is an unusual simplicity to the way the cold fjord water reaches the facility. The intake is designed so that water can enter the cold-water basin through gravity rather than being pumped up from the seabed. Inside the facility, a closed-loop freshwater system circulates through the cooling infrastructure. The same chilled water can continue moving around the data centre without being consumed as part of the cooling process.Once it has absorbed heat through the heat exchanger, the seawater is discharged back into the fjord. Green Mountain says the warmed discharge does not create a negative environmental impact.The company also lists an energy figure for the system of 3 kW of power for 1,000 kW of cooling, illustrating how little electrical energy is needed for the cooling process itself compared with conventional refrigeration.Data centre operators commonly use Power Usage Effectiveness, or PUE, to assess how much energy a facility consumes beyond the electricity delivered directly to its IT equipment. A PUE of 1.0 would mean all the facility's electricity went to computing equipment. Real data centres are higher because they also need power for cooling, lighting, electrical infrastructure, security systems and other supporting equipment.Green Mountain designed its facilities to reach a PUE of 1.2 or lower and says it frequently records values close to 1.10. The company attributes much of this performance to its cooling approach. For comparison, it cites an Uptime Institute average PUE of 1.56 for 2019.Even the electrical infrastructure itself contributes to the figure. UPS systems, which protect servers against power interruptions, lose some energy when converting electricity between forms. Green Mountain estimates that a typical redundant UPS arrangement can add a partial PUE of about 1.06 to 1.10 before transformer losses and other requirements are considered.The fjord water never becomes the air circulating through the server rooms. Heat is transferred through the titanium exchanger, while the chilled freshwater remains in its own circuit. That separation is useful for more than water management. The environment inside the data centre does not have to be exposed directly to outside humidity, pollutants or other contaminants carried in by air.The cooling infrastructure is also duplicated. Green Mountain uses an N+N arrangement, meaning the cooling station, pipework and pumps have redundant counterparts. Both systems can operate during normal conditions, while the design allows maintenance to take place without taking the entire cooling arrangement offline.Under the server-room floor, chilled water is supplied through duplicated routes. The facility can also accommodate different cooling requirements, from conventional server densities to higher-density installations reaching up to 40 kW per square metre.The fjord system relies on relatively few moving components, with circulation pumps doing much of the mechanical work. That reduces the number of parts that require regular servicing compared with a more complicated refrigeration installation.Green Mountain also says the intake location has little algae growth, which helps reduce cleaning requirements for the titanium heat exchanger.The cooling station is connected to the site's data centre infrastructure management system. Its operation is automated, with the system adjusting to changes in demand and continuously reporting its condition.There is also an environmental benefit in avoiding some synthetic refrigerants. Conventional refrigeration systems can rely on gases such as hydrofluorocarbons, which can present an environmental risk if they escape into the atmosphere.Not every data centre has a deep, cold body of water sitting next to it. Green Mountain uses a different form of free cooling at its TEL-Rjukan facility, where the surrounding Norwegian climate provides the cold source.There, an indirect air-cooling system uses outside air to remove heat through a heat exchanger. The air entering the server environment remains in a separate closed circuit, rather than being brought directly into the data rooms.At Rjukan, Green Mountain says the system can provide free cooling for around 330 days a year. The site's median temperature is about 13°C, and its location receives little direct sunlight during part of the year, conditions that help reduce the need for mechanical cooling.During warmer summer periods, water can be introduced on the outside-air side of the cooling equipment. Evaporating that water lowers the temperature available to the cooling system and extends the period in which it can operate efficiently.The Rjukan system was developed with scalability in mind. Its cooling equipment is built in individual units rated at either 250 kW or 500 kW.That means capacity does not have to be installed all at once. As more computing equipment is added, further cooling units can be incorporated into the infrastructure.The approach is also designed around hot-aisle containment, directing heat away from server equipment and allowing the cooling system to deal with it more efficiently. With limited piping and relatively few moving parts, Green Mountain says the design reduces both maintenance requirements and the number of components that could fail.The two Norwegian sites use different natural resources, but the principle is much the same. At Rennesøy, the cooling system takes advantage of water that is already cold. At Rjukan, it makes use of the temperature of the outside air.
Article Summary: Green Mountain uses fjord water to cool its Norwegian data centre. The company says conventional cooling can use up to 80% of the electricity used to power the servers. Instead of making cold mechanically, engineers use naturally chilled water to carry heat away.

Article Title: Meet Meera Ramaswami: The Ann Arbor inventor who turned her grandmother’s fall into a patented mobility device and launched a company
Article Text:
Meera Ramaswami, Founder at CargilityPhoto: Meera Ramaswami/ LinkedIn

A familiar moment with serious consequences

How the device works

Recognition through The Henry Ford

From invention to patent

A mother and daughter become co-founders

The wider need for mobility support

Building an Ann Arbor company

A personal problem becomes a public solution

A fall while getting out of a car changed the direction of Meera Ramaswami’s life. She watched her grandmother lose her balance during a moment that should have been routine, then saw the injury heal while the fear remained. Her grandmother became less willing to travel, and Meera began thinking about how a small loss of stability could lead to isolation and lost independence. That question eventually became Cargility, an Ann Arbor company developing a portable mobility aid that helps people enter and exit vehicles safely. Meera designed the device, tested prototypes, earned recognition through The Henry Ford’s Invention Convention and secured a US utility patent. As reported by The Henry Ford and Ann Arbor SPARK, the invention has grown from a family experience into a company founded by Meera and her mother, Praveena Ramaswami.Getting into or out of a car is an ordinary action for most people, but it can become difficult after an injury, during ageing or for anyone with balance and mobility challenges. A person may need to twist, lower themselves, find a stable surface and stand on uneven ground, all while managing the distance between the seat and pavement.For Meera’s grandmother, that moment led to a fall. The physical injury eventually healed, but the emotional effect lasted longer. Fear of falling again changed how willing she was to leave home. A simple vehicle transfer became a barrier to travel, social connection and independence.Meera recognised that the problem was larger than one family. Older adults, people recovering from surgery or rehabilitation, people with disabilities and caregivers may all face difficulties during vehicle entry and exit. Existing solutions such as walking frames, canes or assistance from another person may not be convenient in the narrow space beside a car. Observation to design Meera began developing the concept in 2022, using a process of observation, prototyping and testing. She didn’t start with an abstract engineering problem, but rather looked at a specific moment in everyday life and asked what kind of support would make it safer. The device needed to be portable, strong and compatible with different passenger vehicles. It also had to be easy enough for a user or caregiver to position without complicated installation. A support that worked only in one type of car would have limited value, so adaptability became an important part of the design.The resulting product, Cargility, is a door to floor mobility assistive device. It engages with the striker in a vehicle’s doorframe and creates a stable support point. An articulating leg reaches the ground, allowing the user to lean on a railing while entering or exiting the vehicle.The design is intended to reduce fall risk and ease the physical strain placed on caregivers. It provides a fixed point of support during the transfer rather than requiring a person to rely on a moving car door or another individual’s strength.The Cargility tool is designed to connect with the striker plate, the metal component in the vehicle doorframe that receives the door latch. Once engaged, the device holds a stable relationship to the vehicle. Its articulating leg consists of two members connected by a pivot, so that the structure can accommodate various vehicle heights and configurations. When positioned correctly, the leg reaches the ground and supports a handrail or bar that the user can hold.The aim is to create a continuous point of stability between the vehicle and the ground. A person can use the rail while lowering into the seat or standing up, reducing the need to twist quickly or search for something to grip.The tool is not intended to replace a doctor, physical therapist or properly prescribed mobility aid. Its purpose is to make one specific part of everyday movement safer and more manageable. The device would still need to be attached correctly and users need to follow the instructions before they can rely on it. Testing and refining the inventionDeveloping the first concept was only the beginning. Meera tested different designs and compared their performance. Earlier descriptions of her work indicate that she created possible models, evaluated them and selected the design that performed best.This kind of testing is central to invention education. A promising idea may fail when exposed to weight, movement, different surfaces or different vehicle shapes.Prototypes expose weaknesses that aren’t apparent on paper. Meera’s work also involved a balancing act between conflicting requirements. The device had to be strong enough to hold a person, but portable enough to carry. It had to fit different cars, but be stable. It had to be easy for users, but not compromise safety. The process required engineering knowledge, but also empathy.A technically impressive device would not be useful if older adults or caregivers found it too complicated. Designing for real people meant considering reach, grip, balance, strength and confidence.Meera’s invention gained recognition through the Invention Convention, a programme supported by The Henry Ford that encourages young people to identify problems and develop solutions. The programme teaches students to move through stages including constructing a prototype, testing it, revising the design and communicating the final idea.In 2022, Meera received top honours in four engineering categories at the Invention Convention held at the Henry Ford Museum.Those awards included innovation, safety, Make the World and the Grand Prize, which provided support for bringing the invention to the US Patent Office.The recognition helped Meera to validate the invention and gain access to a network of mentors, educators and organizations experienced in product development. It also helped turn the project from a student design into an innovation with commercial potential.For young inventors, programmes like the Invention Convention can provide something that classrooms often cannot. They offer a structured way to develop an idea, receive feedback and present it to people who understand engineering and entrepreneurship.Cargility’s mobility concept eventually became a patented technology.Meera Ramaswami was awarded the US patent “Vehicle Access Mobility Tool” in December 2025. The patent describes a device that latches to a vehicle doorframe striker and has an articulating leg attached to the engagement portion. A patent does not mean a product is ready for mass production or on store shelves. It protects the claimed invention and establishes intellectual property rights. It was a major milestone, but more work is needed to make the patented design a reliable product, including manufacturing, testing, regulatory considerations, supply chains and consumer input. It showed that the device had moved beyond a school project and into a formal innovation process. It also created a foundation for building a company around the technology.Meera did not build the company alone. She and her mother, Praveena Ramaswami, became co-founders of Cargility in 2025. Meera continued developing the technical solution, while Praveena left her career to focus full time on the business.The partnership combines engineering and commercial development. Meera understands the design and the problem that inspired it. Praveena has focused on evaluating the mobility ecosystem, building relationships and determining how the company can move toward manufacturing and customers. Starting a company for a physical product is not just having an invention. Founders need to find users, understand the healthcare and mobility market, figure out a pricing model, and decide how the device will be distributed. They must also test the product with the people it is meant to help.The mother daughter structure gives Cargility a personal connection to its mission. The company exists because a family experienced the emotional consequences of a fall and decided to look for a better way.Cargility is aimed at people who may need additional stability during vehicle transfers. That includes older adults, people recovering from rehabilitation and caregivers who help family members get in and out of cars.Vehicle transfers are often overlooked in discussions about accessibility. Public buildings may have ramps and lifts, but the journey begins at home and frequently includes the space between a car seat and the ground. A person may be able to walk once standing but still struggle with the transition.A portable device could be useful for people who travel in different vehicles or do not want permanent equipment installed. It may also help caregivers avoid lifting or pulling, reducing strain on both people.The product’s success will depend on real world testing and user trust. People need confidence that a device will remain secure, work on their vehicle and support them when balance is uncertain.Cargility is part of Ann Arbor’s expanding technology and entrepreneurship ecosystem. The city has programmes that connect founders with mentors, accelerators, university resources and funding opportunities. Ann Arbor SPARK has supported founders through initiatives including Entrepreneur Boot Camp, startup acceleration and other business programmes.For Cargility, that ecosystem can help bridge the gap between invention and commercial launch. Product development may require industrial designers, manufacturing partners, safety experts and investors. Local programmes can connect a small founding team with people who have experience in each area.The company has advanced to a working prototype with design for manufacturing completed and has been targeting an initial small production run and market launch. That stage is important because the best prototype is not always the easiest product to manufacture consistently. A design for manufacturing review helps identify ways to reduce complexity, control cost and maintain quality.Meera’s story began with a private family moment, but the problem she identified is widely shared. Falls can change how older adults and people with mobility limitations view daily activities. Fear can lead to fewer outings, less social contact and greater dependence on others.The Cargility device cannot remove every risk associated with movement. It can, however, address one vulnerable transition with a practical support. The invention shows how innovation often begins when someone pays close attention to an ordinary problem that others have accepted as unavoidable.Its future will depend on continued testing, responsible manufacturing and feedback from users. But the path from grandmother’s fall to patent and company already demonstrates the power of human centred design.Meera did not begin with the intention of becoming a founder. She began by wanting to make one moment safer for someone she loved. That empathy became an engineering question, the question became a prototype and the prototype became Cargility, an Ann Arbor company working to help people move with greater confidence and independence.What are your views on this? Article Title: A US grandfather planned a $100,000-$150,000 treehouse for his grandkids; it grew into a $325,000 backyard castle with a pirate ship and 200-foot zipline
Article Text:
The whimsical design includes a turret, and a pirate ship (Source: Tree Top Builders)

A modest plan that grew far beyond its budget

High-flying features and a pirate ship extension

Expert engineering keeps the play area safe

A fairytale legacy for future generations

What started as a simple plan to build a cozy backyard play area for his grandchildren grew into an impressive architectural project after an American grandfather expanded the idea into a $325,000 custom treehouse complex. According to the Realtor.com, the original budget was between $100,000 and $150,000 for a basic structure. But as new ideas were added, the project continued to grow. Today, the unusual installation looks like a fairytale playground hidden among the trees, complete with a full-size pirate ship and a 200-foot zipline running across the property. The size and detail of the project have turned a private family backyard into a remarkable example of a grandfather’s dedication, combining skilled carpentry with childhood imagination.The original idea was fairly simple. The owner wanted to build a strong, raised play structure where his grandchildren could spend summer afternoons outdoors. But during the early design process, the project quickly became much more ambitious. Instead of choosing a standard wooden platform, the homeowner worked with custom builders to add special architectural features. What began as a small cabin developed into a multi-level structure with sloping roofs, finished loft spaces, custom windows, live-edge cedar siding, and hand-cut cedar shingles.As more features were added, the estimated cost increased sharply. According to the project details, the final price reached $325,000 after high-quality materials, structural engineering reviews, and safety features were included.The main part of the complex is a 12-foot-by-12-foot treehouse raised high above the ground. A tall lookout tower rises above the roof and gives visitors wide views of the surrounding garden. The main treehouse was first connected to a separate wooden platform by an open-air rope bridge. However, the owner decided that a simple observation deck was not exciting enough for his growing grandchildren. The second platform was then rebuilt and turned into a large pirate ship extension. According to the project details, it includes play cannons, nautical ropes and equipment, and wooden decks designed around the pirate theme. For even more adventure, an octagonal launch platform was built beside the main treehouse. From there, riders can attach themselves to a 200-foot zipline that carries them through the trees to a special landing tower inspired by Rapunzel’s castle.Building such a large treehouse required more than basic do-it-yourself skills. Custom treehouse engineers were brought in to make sure the structures were safe for children and did not damage the trees supporting them. According to Tree Top Builders, the company involved in creating the aerial design, “Building a treehouse is easy, but building a safe, long-lasting, tree-friendly treehouse requires expertise. ” The company also said, “We work with the tree, not against it.” Arborists and structural engineers worked together to create flexible attachment systems. These systems allow the trees to move naturally during strong winds and continue growing without being restricted by heavy support beams. According to the project information, the interiors were finished with smooth wooden walls and strong safety railings, creating a secure space for children to use throughout the year.Although the final cost was much higher than the original budget, the project created a unique family space that has become a centerpiece for gatherings. The $325,000 backyard treehouse is more than an elaborate playground. According to the project details, it was designed to remain useful as the grandchildren grow into teenagers and young adults. The finished lofts provide flexible areas for relaxing and spending time together, while the strong construction is designed to keep the complex standing for many years. What began as a simple backyard project has therefore become a lasting family attraction, combining adventure, craftsmanship, and a grandfather’s desire to create something special for future generations.
Article Summary: An American grandfather built a $325,000 treehouse complex for his grandchildren. The original plan was to build a simple play area for the children. But as more features were added, the cost of the project increased sharply. The complex includes a pirate ship, play cannons, and a 200-foot zipline.

Article Title: In 2023, a California materials scientist built a device that pulled drinking water from desert air; it produced 35 litres a day at just 20% humidity
Article Text:
AI Representation: A device collects drinking water from dry desert air and fills a reservoir with fresh water. Image credits: Chatgpt

The harvester ran on ambient sunlight alone

How the output shifted with humidity

An earlier MOF proved the concept could work at 20 percent humidity

Why dry air poses the harder engineering challenge

From a two-hand prototype toward household-scale units

In the summer of 2023, scientists from UC Berkeley took a machine that could be held by two hands to Death Valley National Park in North America, which is one of the most arid and hot locations on the continent and allowed it to operate using only the energy of the sun. It pulled water vapor out of the desert air, converted it to liquid and produced drinkable water without a battery, a plug, or any moving parts drawing outside power. The chemist behind the work, Omar Yaghi, had spent years building toward that single field test.This device uses a MOF, or metal-organic framework, an ultra-porous crystalline structure that Yaghi's team has studied for years. The specific MOF used here is MOF-303, an aluminum MOF that captures water molecules from the air at night, when humidity is usually higher in the desert and releases them during the day as sunlight warms the material. The resulting vapor condenses on a cooler surface within the device and flows into a container.Testing the same device in two very different climates allowed the team to isolate the effect of humidity.In Death Valley, the harvester achieved up to 210 grams of water per kilogram of MOF-303 per day in a single day-and-night cycle, marking the highest output the team recorded at that site. By comparison, in the milder, more humid air of Berkeley, the same device reached up to 285 grams per kilogram per day under similar passive operation, though Berkeley's daily averages ran lower on some days. The results appear in a 2023 paper in Nature Water , MOF water harvester produces water from Death Valley desert air in ambient sunlight, by Woochul Song, Zhiling Zheng, Ali Alawadhi and Yaghi, and they mark roughly double what an earlier passive version of the harvester had managed.Death Valley’s new technology is a further development of the tests done on the material by Yaghi and his team six years back, in collaboration with mechanical engineers from MIT. This project, which was done in 2017, involved a totally new material made up of zirconium and referred to as MOF-801. The results proved that even at low humidity levels between 20% and 30%, a solar-driven water harvester could generate significant quantities of water.The findings, published in Science as Water harvesting from air with metal-organic frameworks powered by natural sunlight, reported a yield of about 2.8 liters of water per kilogram of MOF per day at relative humidity as low as 20 percent, using only sunlight to drive the release step; some press accounts described the same result as roughly 2.8 liters over a 12-hour test window, though the paper itself reports it as a daily figure. The 2023 Nature Water study notes that switching from zirconium-based MOF-801, priced at $160 per kilogram, to aluminum-based MOF-303, priced at $3 per kilogram, made the harvester far cheaper to build; the higher water yield came from MOF-303's own adsorption behavior, not from its lower price.Water extraction from moist air is fairly easy since most dehumidifiers function on the principle of cooling air below its dew point. Nevertheless, air in the desert presents a different challenge. This is because at relative humidity less than 20%, the dew point may be below the freezing point, meaning that a lot of energy will be required for the process of condensation. MOFs are designed such that their pores are capable of adsorbing water molecules, even at very low levels of humidity, while heat can desorb them.The Death Valley test was, by design, a proof‑of‑concept prototype rather than a final, household‑scale product. The scientists pointed out that the tiny size and limited daily amount of water provided by the device were more appropriate for proving the concept behind the chemical reaction rather than for providing enough drinking water for a family's daily needs. Yaghi also disclosed in a public interview that further development along the same lines of MOF chemistry greatly enhanced production, and his firm began manufacturing more efficient devices capable of producing water in quantities of dozens or even hundreds of liters each day.
Article Summary: Device uses a MOF, or metal-organic framework, an ultra-porous crystalline structure that Yaghi's team has studied for years. The specific MOF used is MOF-303, an aluminum MOF that captures water molecules from the air at night and releases them during the day as sunlight warms the material. The resulting vapor condenses on a cooler surface within the device and flows into a container.

Article Title: Tourists leave behind “lint bunnies” inside the world’s longest cave; volunteers have removed about 600 pounds of human debris
Article Text:
Image AI generated

Why is lint a problem in Mammoth Cave

How does Mammoth Cave collect and remove lint

How do volunteers clean lint from Mammoth Cave

Image AI generated

Visitors to Mammoth Cave may expect to leave with memories of its vast underground passages, but they also leave something far less welcome behind. Fibres from clothing, strands of hair and tiny pieces of rubbish gradually collect along the routes through the world’s longest cave system, forming small balls nicknamed “lint bunnies”. The debris is more than an eyesore: it can encourage microbial growth, affect cave formations and settle on historic artefacts. To tackle the problem, volunteers from the National Speleological Society return to the cave with brooms and HEPA vacuums, carefully removing the human debris. Over the years, their efforts have collected about 600 pounds.The work requires patience because volunteers must avoid disturbing fragile cave surfaces and formations while removing debris from heavily visited areas. Their efforts help preserve Mammoth Cave’s unusual underground environment and protect its natural and cultural features for future visitors.According to the National Park Service, lint can affect the cave ecosystem because it introduces additional food into an environment that is naturally poor in food. It can also contribute to microbial growth and even dissolve formations. In addition, accumulated material can discolour cave features, including rocks, walls and flowstone.Mammoth Cave is not only a natural environment but also contains cultural resources. Lint can settle on artefacts that are hundreds or thousands of years old, potentially causing damage. It can also cover historic signatures along the tour routes, obscuring evidence left behind by earlier visitors and cave users. What may appear to tourists as little more than fluff therefore has consequences for both the cave’s natural and cultural features.To reduce the amount of material reaching the cave walls, the park has installed short boards along sections of the touring trails. These are known as “lint rails” and are designed to collect fibres before they can settle on rocks and walls. Some of the material also falls into cracks in the paved trail, where it gathers into the small formations that gave the phenomenon its memorable name: “lint bunnies”.The debris has accumulated on the rails and paved surfaces; it is physical. The National Park Service shows volunteers using both brooms and high-efficiency particulate air, or HEPA, vacuums along the cave’s tour routes. The cleaning is therefore a hands-on conservation effort carried out without preventing visitors from continuing to experience the cave.The clean-up effort grew out of cooperation between Mammoth Cave National Park and the National Speleological Society (NSS). The Mammoth Cave Restoration Camp organises three weekend camps and one weeklong camp each year, giving volunteers a chance to help remove dirt and lint while keeping the cave accessible to visitors. The NPS says the volunteer group known as the Lint Bunnies has existed for about 12 years and continues to help maintain the cave for thousands of visitors.Initially, the volunteers used simple brooms and dustpans and did their work once a year during the weeklong Restoration Camp. As their methods and equipment improved, the programme expanded, allowing participants to sign up for daily lint-cleaning tasks. The NPS says improvements to paved trails have enabled the clean-up to continue for as many as five days at a time, while each crew is limited to six people to reduce disruption to daily cave tours.Using brooms or HEPA vacuums, volunteers now search out the material visitors leave behind. According to the National Park Service, the crews have collected approximately 600 pounds of lint and other items left behind by tours over the years. That figure turns an apparently trivial form of litter into a striking measure of the human footprint inside one of the world's most remarkable underground environments.
Article Summary: Fibres from clothing, strands of hair and tiny pieces of rubbish gradually collect along the routes through the world’s longest cave system. The debris is more than an eyesore: it can encourage microbial growth, affect cave formations and settle on historic artefacts. To tackle the problem, volunteers from the National Speleological Society return to the cave with brooms and HEPA vacuums.

Article Title: Phoenix turned shipping containers into 40 private transitional homes for homeless seniors; each 160-sq-ft unit has a bathroom, and 56 permanent apartments are planned next
Article Text:
From shipping containers to private rooms

What comes next?

The city of Phoenix has decided to tackle homelessness with a new method. What was once designed to carry goods across oceans is now serving a very different purpose in Phoenix, Arizona: giving older people experiencing homelessness a private place to sleep, shower and begin rebuilding their lives.The city recently opened a new project offering a transitional housing community made from shipping containers for older adults facing homelessness. On Wednesday, city officials gathered for the opening of Senior Bridge, which provides 40 individual transitional housing units for adults aged 55 and older who are experiencing homelessness and need light-touch support as they work toward permanent housing. It is located at 28th and Van Buren streets. The collaboration is between the City of Phoenix and the Arizona Department of Housing and is operated by Mercy House.Each unit measures just 160 square feet, but it is designed to function as a self-contained living space. Residents have a bed, sink, toilet, shower, microwave and small refrigerator. The project is operated by Mercy House in partnership with the City of Phoenix and the Arizona Department of Housing.The City of Phoenix contributed $750,000 toward the 40-unit first phase. It is also investing another $9.6 million in the project's second phase, which is planned to provide 56 affordable housing units.At first glance, the Senior Bridge units look more like an industrial experiment than conventional housing. The containers have been modified into compact private rooms, with basic amenities built into the limited space. Unlike a traditional emergency shelter, however, residents have their own individual units and private bathrooms.The first phase opened on March 25, 2026, at 28th and Van Buren streets in Phoenix. The 40 units are intended for people aged 55 and older who are experiencing homelessness and are capable of living independently with limited support. The small footprint is part of what makes the project distinctive. Each 160-square-foot unit is roughly comparable in floor area to a small bedroom plus bathroom, yet it contains the essentials needed for someone to live there temporarily.The entire complex is designed to run on solar power, with lithium battery storage. According to Mercy House chief program officer Timothy Huynh, the site can operate completely off the electrical grid. That feature could be particularly relevant in Phoenix, where extremely hot summers can place enormous demands on electricity infrastructure. The solar-and-battery system also gives the development an element of resilience while reducing its dependence on conventional grid power.Mercy House officials told Axios that there is no fixed maximum length of stay, but residents are ideally expected to move on to permanent housing within about 90 days. Each resident is paired with a case manager who can help connect them with healthcare, nutrition assistance and community services. Those services are important because the project is designed as a bridge rather than simply a place to sleep.People experiencing homelessness are not a single group, and older adults can face particular challenges when trying to move from the street or a shelter into stable housing. Senior Bridge specifically targets adults 55 and older who need a safe and stable place while they work toward permanent accommodation. The city describes the development as transitional housing for people who need relatively light support rather than intensive residential care. The idea is to give residents enough stability to address the barriers that may have contributed to their homelessness while simultaneously working toward their next housing option.The 40 shipping-container units are only the first stage of the Senior Bridge project. The second phase is planned to add 56 permanent supportive apartments, significantly larger than the temporary units. The apartments are expected to be around 750 square feet each, according to Axios, and residents will pay affordable rent while not having to pay power bills. Construction of the container-based apartments was underway, with residents expected to begin moving in around early December.That means the development is being designed to provide a pathway between temporary and longer-term housing rather than treating transitional accommodation as the final solution.The city has also highlighted Senior Bridge as part of its broader response to homelessness. Its Office of Homeless Solutions lists the project as providing 40 units of transitional housing for seniors aged 55 and older, with a future phase of permanent supportive housing.
Article Summary: The city of Phoenix recently opened a new project offering a transitional housing community made from shipping containers for older adults facing homelessness. Each unit measures just 160 square feet, but it is designed to function as a self-contained living space. Residents have a bed, sink, toilet, shower, microwave and small refrigerator. The project is operated by Mercy House in partnership with the City of Phoenix and the Arizona Department of Housing.

Article Title: In 1949, Pennsylvania shoe salesman Mahlon Haines built a 25-foot-tall work-boot house for $26,000; after falling into ruin, his granddaughter restored it and guests can now sleep inside
Article Text:
A shoe salesman turned advertising into architecture

From honeymoon getaway to ice-cream parlour

His granddaughter brought the Shoe House back

You can now sleep inside the giant boot

What began as an audacious advertising idea for a Pennsylvania shoe businessman in the 1940s is now a roadside landmark where visitors can actually spend the night. The Haines Shoe House, a 25-foot-tall building shaped like a work boot, was built by shoe entrepreneur Mahlon Haines and today operates as a short-term rental. According to the Haines Shoe House’s official history, construction began in 1948 and the first guests arrived in 1949. The building cost $26,000 at the time. The Library of Congress also dates its construction to 1948-49. Located in Hellam Township, near York, the unusual structure measures about 48 feet long, 17 feet wide and 25 feet high. Its design was deliberately shaped like a high-topped work shoe, making it an early example of what architects describe as programmatic architecture, buildings designed to resemble or directly represent the purpose, product or idea they are associated with.Haines, known locally as the “Shoe Wizard”, built the house as a promotional attraction for his shoe business. Rather than simply putting up another sign, he created a building that could hardly be missed by people travelling through the area.The shoe theme extends beyond its exterior. Inside, the rooms are arranged within different parts of the boot, with the living room occupying the toe, the kitchen in the heel, bedrooms in the ankle and a recreation area in the instep.The building also features shoe-themed details, including stained glass. But Haines did not build the enormous shoe as his own home.The Shoe House was originally used as a guest house. Haines made it available to elderly couples celebrating anniversaries and, for a period, honeymooning couples connected to towns where his stores operated. After Haines died in 1962, the property passed to his employees, who sold it in 1964. It subsequently spent years as a tourist attraction and ice-cream parlour, drawing visitors curious to see what a life-sized shoe looked like from the inside. Over time, however, the landmark fell into disrepair.In 1987, Haines’ granddaughter, Annie Haines Keller, bought the deteriorating property and began restoring it. The restoration brought the Shoe House back into use as a historic attraction and helped preserve an unusual piece of Pennsylvania’s roadside history.The property changed hands several more times over the following decades, with successive owners carrying out repairs and preservation work. In 2022, it was sold to Waylon and Naomi Brown, who gave the building further improvements and converted its use into a short-term rental.The Shoe House is no longer open for ordinary public tours. Instead, registered guests can rent the entire property for groups of up to six people. The roughly 1,500-square-foot building has three bedrooms, two-and-a-half bathrooms, a living room, kitchen/dinette and recreation room spread across its unusual five levels. Narrow staircases connect the spaces, adding another reminder that this is less a conventional house than a piece of architectural theatre.The landmark also received a Pennsylvania state historical marker in 2023, formally recognising its place in the state’s history. More than seven decades after Mahlon Haines turned a work boot into an advertising spectacle, the idea still works. The building remains impossible to mistake for anything else, and, for those who book a stay, the giant shoe is no longer just something to photograph from the road. It is a place to sleep.
Article Summary: The Haines Shoe House is a 25-foot-tall building shaped like a work boot. It was built by shoe entrepreneur Mahlon Haine and cost $26,000 to build. It is now a roadside landmark where visitors can actually spend the night.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.
